title: review follow-ups of PR #34565 (readableIdsLeaf refusal): refusal message, bit TSDoc and ADR-0139 note, cli/lint comments, read-scope id source
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQ2SN4K183oqAvUajA

Filing gate ②: the four wording nits the contract review of PR #34565 (merged; Fixes #33876) carried as follow-ups: comments 6937856418, 6941313688, 6942192439. Dedupe: `readableIdsLeaf refusal wording`; no open card.

Suggested-grade: p3 · domain:server · documentation

## Items

- N2 — the where-refusal message says a declaring driver runs the nested-relation condition as one statement. `driver-memory` evaluates it in process, and the named fallbacks keep the id read. Say what each path does.
- N3 — the TSDoc of the `readableIdsLeaf` bit (and the ADR-0139 amendment that landed with #34565) say the condition is planned as the leaf when the bit is `true` and that a lookup dimension is refused without it. The first omits the fallbacks `relation-semi-join.ts` names; the second holds only where the host bridges the engine. Correct both in one pass.
- N8 — the new cli and lint comments name the refused condition more widely than the function refuses it: the refusal is for a condition beneath a single-valued relation on a read verb. The cli comment omits "single-valued"; the lint comment omits that and the read verb. Match the changeset and the contract docblock.
- N9 — the changeset route for a read scope, "`account` `$in` the ids it may read", does not say where a policy gets those ids. A read scope cannot run the two-step read the entries above describe, so the author holds the ids in the scope or keys the scope on a field of the object. Add that clause where the guidance is published (the changeset itself is released; carry it into the docs that teach the route).

No behaviour change; text only. The ADR-0139 edit is governed (`docs/adr/**`), so that line lands Tier H.
